problem_framing.rationale: The decision is framed exactly as posed (enter or not, and by which route). All five board objectives and constraints are listed on slide 2 and reused as the comparison criteria on slide 29. The issue the answer turns on, ad cost against payback, is named in the governing thought, and the scope exclusions (mass, DTC, acquisition) are stated and justified. Nothing material to fix.

storyline_coherence.rationale: The governing thought answers the question, the five summary points map one-to-one to the sections, and almost every title is a claim that its slide's evidence supports. The flaws are redundancy and one overstated title. Each section opens with a slide (5, 12, 19, 27) that restates the slides that follow, and the contents slide appears five times. The titles of slides 27 and 29 say Option A 'meets/passes' the payback test without the ACoS condition that the deck's own slides 15–16 show is decisive; the condition appears only in the verdict cell and footnote. The competitor slide sits a little awkwardly inside the Option B section.

evidence_and_reasoning.rationale: I re-derived every key figure and they match the pack and the key. Amazon contribution is $10.73 before ads and $4.73 / $4.01 / $3.05 at 25% / 28% / 32% ACoS; retail is $7.545. Option A cumulative cash is +2.40 / +0.38 / −2.32, break-even ACoS is 28.6%, and the tariff cases are −0.7 and −3.4. Option B peaks at $20.8M on plan inputs ($26.4M at 2.6 units with no halo), and group margin is 4.5% in 2027. Japan ends at +$1.8M. Derivations are transparent and evidence against the recommendation (32% benchmark, stalled Amazon-first brands, repeat below Korea) is used. It falls short of a 5 on several small points. The interquartile range is misread ('top quarter… at most 3.4'). 'Demand is proven' and 'Demand is not the limit' overstate a six-month, three-SKU pilot when the 2027 plan needs 1.8 times the June run-rate. Mooncrest's awareness and 'ad cost and repeat decide who scales' are asserted without pack support. There is no volume downside case, and market growth is given as a 1.9x multiple and a one-year rate rather than a CAGR.

strategic_judgment.rationale: The recommendation is clear and defensible: Amazon-led entry, ambition reset to about $26M, and a retail gate raised to 20% awareness with test doors and a 4.0 units sell-through check. All three options are compared on the board's own tests, the main trade-offs are explicit, and no trap is fallen into. There is a scorecard with thresholds, owners and a dated review. The gaps are in what happens when the central condition fails. The deck's own evidence says scaling brands run at a 32% median ACoS, yet the scorecard gives no action if ACoS exceeds 28.6% (the 'if missed' cell only restates the consequence). There is no stop or exit criterion and no statement of whether the board should accept a fifth-year payback. The tension that a hard ACoS ceiling may cost the plan's volumes is not addressed, and a lower fixed-cost variant to widen the payback margin is not explored. The 28.6% threshold also depends on untested plan volumes.

clarity_and_concision.rationale: The answer is on slide 3 and the language is plain and precise. But 45 slides and about 7,000 words is substantially more than this decision needs. There are five repeated contents slides, four section-summary slides that duplicate the slides after them, and several appendix slides that restate body numbers. False precision (994,035.8 units, 17.97%) adds noise.

unsupported_claims.quote: Demand is proven, and it is still climbing
unsupported_claims.why: A six-month, three-SKU cross-border pilot at a 168,000-unit run-rate does not prove demand for a plan that needs 300,000 units in 2027 and 1.1 million in 2030; the deck itself lists volume as a KPI to re-base.

unsupported_claims.quote: Demand is not the limit; the ambition's timing is
unsupported_claims.why: The pack has no evidence that demand is unconstrained or that $40M would be reached later; planning volumes are untested forecasts.

unsupported_claims.quote: Entered 450 doors before building awareness and was off the shelves two years later
unsupported_claims.why: The pack gives Mooncrest's route, door count, removal and loss, but nothing about its awareness level or why it failed.

unsupported_claims.quote: Ad cost and repeat decide who scales
unsupported_claims.why: This is a causal lesson attached to Gaon Lab and Yeoreum; the pack gives no reason why those brands stayed below $5M.

unsupported_claims.quote: The 0.71 correlation between doors and Amazon sales does not prove a halo — large Amazon brands win the doors
unsupported_claims.why: The first half is valid, but the title asserts the reverse causal direction as fact; the pack supports only that causality is unproven (the body text is better calibrated with 'more likely').

unsupported_claims.quote: K-beauty facial skincare sales nearly doubled in four years and took share from every other kind of brand
unsupported_claims.why: The pack gives only K-beauty against the total; 'every other kind of brand' cannot be derived from one aggregate remainder.

unsupported_claims.quote: Helps paid traffic convert as keywords broaden
unsupported_claims.why: The effect of the review base on ad conversion is not in the pack; it is general knowledge presented as a finding.

numerical_errors.quote: Top quarter of that band: still at most 3.4 units a door, under the cut-off
numerical_errors.correct: 3.4 is the upper bound of the interquartile range, i.e. the 75th percentile. Three-quarters of brands in the band sell at most 3.4; the top quarter sells 3.4 or more and some may exceed 4.0.

recommendation.summary: Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon (Option A) under an ACoS ceiling near 28.6%. Reject the national retail launch. Defer the Japan decision to 2028. Restate the ambition as about $26M by 2030. Add specialty retail only after a gate of $10M Amazon sales and 20% aided awareness, starting with test doors that must reach 4.0 units per door per week.
recommendation.rationale: It meets all four defensibility criteria. Options are compared on cap, payback and margin floor. The 25% ACoS and 4.5 units per door assumptions are tested against the 32% and 2.6 benchmarks. The condition for payback (ACoS at or below 28.6%, plan volumes, duty at 15%) is stated with a scorecard and review date. It says plainly that $40M is not reachable by 2030 on either route. The weakness is that it sets no explicit action or exit rule if ACoS runs above the ceiling.

hypothesis_handling.rationale: The deck keeps the CEO's Amazon-first route but conditions it on an ACoS ceiling of 28.6%, which it derives, and resets the $40M ambition to about $26M. It tightens the CEO's retail trigger from 15% to 20% awareness, with test doors and a 4.0 units check, grounded in Table 8 and the delisting threshold. It confronts the 25% ACoS plan with the 32% benchmark, the 4.5 units assumption with the 2.6 median, and the halo memo with reverse causality. This matches the expected handling. The shortfalls are that it does not say what to do if the ACoS condition fails, and it makes two causal assertions the pack does not support (the direction of the doors–Amazon link stated as fact in a title, and why the stalled brands stalled).

output.overall_comment: Strong, numerically rigorous work: every required calculation reproduces (unit economics, Option A payback by ACoS and tariff, 28.6% break-even, Option B's $20.8M peak and 4.5% group margin, Japan's +$1.8M). All critical evidence is used, including evidence against the recommendation, and no trap is fallen into. The recommendation matches the key's preferred answer, with sensible gates and a reset ambition. The material weaknesses are: no consequence or exit rule if ACoS exceeds the ceiling, even though the deck's own benchmark says 32% is typical; no volume downside case or lower-fixed-cost variant; a few overstated claims ('demand is proven', Mooncrest's awareness, an interquartile-range misread); and a length of 45 slides with repeated contents and section-summary slides. Weighted score is about 4.05.
